title: Complementary events
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:38Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank teaches complementary events; the probability points cover sample spaces, Venn diagrams, conditional and independent events, but none teaches P(not A) = 1 − P(A) as its main idea.

draft.title: Complementary events
card: The complement of an event is the event not happening. If A is rain tomorrow, the complement of A is no rain tomorrow.
An event and its complement cover every outcome, and they cannot both happen. So their probabilities add to 1.
P(not A) = 1 − P(A). Probabilities can be written as fractions, decimals or percentages, and 1 means 100%.
Example: the chance a bus is late is 0.15. The chance it is not late is 1 − 0.15 = 0.85.
draft.remember: To find the chance of something not happening, take its probability away from 1.

a.q: The probability that Ravi's train is on time is 0.92. What is the probability that it is not on time?
a.why: P(not on time) = 1 − 0.92 = 0.08. The value 0.92 is the chance of the train being on time, not the complement. Adding to 1 instead of taking away gives 1.92, which is impossible for a probability.
a.clue: The two probabilities must add to 1.

b.q: A spinner at a school fair has a 3/8 chance of landing on red. What is the probability that it does not land on red?
b.why: P(not red) = 1 − 3/8 = 8/8 − 3/8 = 5/8. The option 3/5 compares red with not red, which is not a probability of not red. A probability can never be larger than 1, so 8/3 cannot be right.
b.clue: Write 1 as a fraction with 8 on the bottom.
